# Blueprints and fields

A blueprint is the form an editor fills in, and the shape the stored data is validated against. It is tabs,
sections and fields:

```yaml
title: Guide
tabs:
  main:
    display: Content
    sections:
      - fields:
          - handle: body
            field: { type: rich_text, display: Body }
          - handle: region
            field: { type: terms, taxonomy: regions, max: 1 }
```

## Fieldtypes

| Group | Types |
|---|---|
| Text | `text`, `textarea`, `rich_text`, `slug`, `secret` |
| Numbers and dates | `integer`, `date` |
| Choice | `select`, `radio`, `checkboxes`, `toggle`, `list` |
| Relationships | `entries`, `terms`, `relationship`, `link` |
| Files | `assets`, `files` |
| Repeating | `grid`, `replicator` |
| Whole-page | `seo` |

`replicator` and `grid` hold repeating groups of fields; a replicator's **sets** render through
`themes/<yours>/views/sets/<type>.vue`, which is how a page built of blocks works.

A `fieldset` is a group of fields imported into more than one blueprint, so a shared set of SEO or contact fields
is written once.

## Generated types

Every blueprint contributes to `themes/<yours>/.nibble/types.d.ts`, so a view has real types for the fields it
renders. It is regenerated by the generators and by `bin/rails nibble:schema:types`, and `nibble:check` fails if
it is stale.
